cards.explanation: The answer is the kings and all the people. The LORD says, "Hear the word of the LORD, O kings of Judah, all people of Judah and Jerusalem who enter through these gates." (Jeremiah 17:20) Kings and the people of Judah and Jerusalem get the very same message, friends. Nobody gets a side door.

The answer is False. The LORD says, "Go and stand at the gate of the people, through which the kings of Judah go in and out; and stand at all the other gates of Jerusalem." (Jeremiah 17:19) So it's the gate of the people AND all the others. That's a whole lot of gates for one prophet, friends.

The answer is carry a load through them. The LORD says, "do not carry a load or bring it through the gates of Jerusalem on the Sabbath day." (Jeremiah 17:21) The warning is about loads coming through those gates, bakers. Even a heavy day of hauling had to stop for the Sabbath.

The answer is True. The LORD says, "You must not carry a load out of your houses or do any work on the Sabbath day…" (Jeremiah 17:22) So the rule reaches right into people's homes, friends. No sneaking a load out the back door either.

The answer is keep it holy. The LORD says, "…but you must keep the Sabbath day holy, just as I commanded your forefathers." (Jeremiah 17:22) No loads and no work, and the day is kept holy. That's the command, friends, plain and simple.

The answer is False. The LORD says, "Yet they would not listen or incline their ear, but they stiffened their necks and would not listen or receive My discipline." (Jeremiah 17:23) The forefathers heard the command and would not listen, friends. That's a rough report card.

The answer is True. The LORD says that if they listen and keep the Sabbath day holy, "…then kings and princes will enter through the gates of this city." (Jeremiah 17:25) They ride in with their officials, too, bakers. The gates would be busy in the best way.
The answer is forever. The LORD says, "…this city will be inhabited forever." (Jeremiah 17:25) That's the promise if the people listen, friends. Forever is a long time to keep the lights on.

The answer is offerings. The LORD says people will come "…bringing burnt offerings and sacrifices, grain offerings and frankincense, and thank offerings to the house of the LORD." (Jeremiah 17:26) That's if the people listen, friends. They come from the cities of Judah and the places around Jerusalem with their gifts.

The answer is the citadels of Jerusalem. The LORD says He will "…kindle an unquenchable fire in its gates to consume the citadels of Jerusalem." (Jeremiah 17:27) The fire starts at the gates and the citadels are what it consumes, bakers. It's a heavy warning, and the LORD says it plainly.
